title: Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks
layout_note: Four steps labelled a) to d) under one wide strip: a) a training image plane with a camera and a ray passing through a sparse 3-D grid of coloured dots, one voxel highlighted as a translucent blue cube; b) that cube enlarged by a light-blue zoom wedge into a dashed cube whose eight corner spheres (spherical-harmonic balls) send yellow arrows to the sample point on the ray, with a row of SH glyphs and a Sum sign above; c) a dotted curved arrow to a sigma-vs-ray-distance plot and a 'Predicted Color' swatch; d) the objective 'minimize L_recon + lambda L_TV' as an equation.
grouping: No boxes or containers; the four steps are separated only by whitespace and named by a) - d) sub-labels underneath. The zoom wedge from the highlighted voxel to the enlarged cube is the only grouping device.
shapes_depth: Rendered 3-D illustration: a perspective dashed wire grid with coloured voxel dots, translucent blue cube, shaded spheres textured with spherical-harmonic colour patterns, a thick black ray arrow, a light-blue gradient zoom cone; step c is a small 2-D line plot with a green-to-blue curve and a teal colour square.
proposed_highlight: The representation is the visual centre: the sparse voxel grid and its zoomed cell with SH spheres take most of the width, while rendering and optimization are a small plot and an equation at the right.
lesson: Zoom from one cell of the scene representation into an enlarged copy with a translucent wedge, and show the per-sample computation (trilinear weights) as coloured arrows inside the enlarged cell before handing off to a small plot and the loss equation.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; no venue printed on the arXiv first page; remembered venue CVPR 2022 (not verified).

arrangement.units: four unframed steps in one horizontal strip, separated by whitespace and named by sub-labels a) Sparse Voxel Grid, b) Trilinear Interpolation, c) Volumetric Rendering, d) Optimization
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo (a plant) on a tilted image plane with a camera glyph, labelled 'Training Image'
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right, as a typeset 'minimize L_recon + lambda L_TV' equation under the rendering plot, with no arrow to it
arrangement.shared: the ray is one continuous black arrow drawn again in the zoomed cube

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis / radiance field optimization
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = an explicit sparse voxel grid storing density and spherical-harmonic coefficients, with no neural network

core.what: a ray through a sparse voxel grid, with one cell opened into an enlarged cube where yellow arrows interpolate the eight corner spherical-harmonic values onto the sample point, then rendering and optimisation at the right

relations.form: a shaded blue cell in the sparse grid widens through a pale blue wedge into the enlarged dashed cube of panel b, the ray drawn again through it
panel a draws the method on its data: a real plant photo on a tilted image plane with a camera glyph, the ray through a dashed wire grid of coloured voxel dots
in panel b eight yellow arrows from the cube corners converge on one sample point on the ray; a sigma-sum arrow brings a palette of spherical-harmonic spheres into a corner
four sub-labelled steps a) to d) in one horizontal strip: grid, interpolation, a 2-D density-vs-distance plot with a predicted colour swatch, and an optimisation objective
a dotted curved arrow carries the ray from panel b to the rendering plot, whose arrow leads to the predicted colour

channels.colour: voxel and corner colours = the stored per-voxel values (spheres shaded as SH colour); yellow = interpolation weights; blue = the zoomed cell and wedge; the SH palette groups red, green, blue bands
channels.shape: dots on a wire grid = voxels, shaded spheres = SH coefficients, curve plot = density along ray, square = predicted colour
channels.line: solid black = ray, yellow arrows = interpolation, dotted curved = hand-off to rendering, dashed grey = voxel edges
channels.frame: none; steps separated by whitespace and sub-labels

quality.strengths: The contribution, a voxel grid with trilinear interpolation instead of an MLP, is the biggest element and is drawn on its own structure, with the zoom wedge tying the enlarged cell to the grid; interpolation is shown as arrows converging on the sample rather than described.
quality.weaknesses: The objective in d) is a typeset equation with no arrow from the rendered colour; the dotted hand-off from b) to c) arcs up and over; colour carries both voxel values and the separate yellow interpolation weights and blue zoom tint, and the rendering curve's colours are not tied to the grid.

insights.structure: A single left-to-right strip of four steps, where the first two are one 3-D scene (grid then zoomed cell) and the last two shrink to a 2-D plot and an equation at the right edge.
insights.data: The input is a real photo on a perspective image plane, the voxels are coloured dots on a dashed wire grid, the SH coefficients are a palette of shaded spheres, and the rendered output is a single teal colour swatch.
insights.emphasis: The translucent blue voxel and its light-blue zoom cone pull the eye to the enlarged cell, where yellow arrows from the eight corner spheres converge on the sample point.
insights.flow: The camera ray runs as one thick black arrow through the grid and on through the zoomed cube; a dotted curved arrow then jumps up and right to the rendering plot, and step d has no arrow at all.
insights.avoid: The optimization step d is detached text with no arrow back to the voxels, so the loop that trains the grid is not drawn.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
